messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-api.us-west-2 p99 latency spike detected (3.6s) — error rate 0.8% — routing to #incidents for on-call
Sarah: oncall here, seeing paging. grabbing console now. any customer-facing escalations?
Priya (support): Just opened a support ticket, customer 'Voltix' reporting paused streams and UI timeouts. Ticket ID: SUP-2247. Notified account team.
David: I can join. initial glance at infra metrics — host gw45 and gw46 show nvme io wait spikes and cgroup blkio throttling on GPU shared pool.
Linh: streaming tail traces show a bunch of requests stuck at "write_to_socket" after model token generation — looks like backpressure from the host network/IO. p95 moved from 220ms -> 1.8s, p99 -> 3.6s.
Omar: tagging noisy-tenant hypothesis. which tenant has ramped up? top consumers: tenant-id t-88 (batch rerank jobs) and t-212 (large chat sessions). both on shared-gpu-pool-02.
Sarah: ok primary mitigation plan: 1) throttle heavy tenants 2) offload long-running batches to dedicated queue 3) if needed, evacuate busiest containers to spare hosts. we need quick mitigations to restore streaming SLOs.
David: pushing a lightweight QoS throttle via cgroup for t-88 and t-212 now. command:
```bash
# on gw45
cgexec -g blkio:/tenant_t88 /bin/true
echo "8:0 1048576" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant_t88/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device
echo "8:0 1048576" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant_t88/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
# repeat for tenant_t212
```
Linh: mirrored policy applied to gw46. also enabling ephemeral prefix caching offload for streaming endpoints to reduce KV pressure: `service kv-cache set --namespace streaming --mode readonly`
Sarah: Priya, please update Voltix that we're investigating and applying mitigation; ask them if they have any in-flight long-running jobs.
Priya (support): Sent note: "We're throttling noisy background jobs and prioritizing low-latency streams; will update in 10m." Voltix replied: "Seeing partial recovery, some sessions still stall."
IncidentBot: Metric update (5m): p95=1.1s p99=2.9s error=0.4% — improvement after throttles.
Omar: Good signal. But I still see intermittent streaming stalls tied to KV cache evictions and GPU memory thrash on t-212 tasks. trace snippet (truncated):
```text
TRACE id=0x7f3c.. host=gw45 container=c-9a3d step=kv_lookup duration=260ms
TRACE id=0x7f3c.. host=gw45 container=c-9a3d step=model_infer duration=1900ms
TRACE id=0x7f3c.. host=gw45 container=c-9a3d step=socket_write duration=800ms status=EPIPE
```
David: That model_infer 1900ms looks like GPU stalls — could be kernel contention. I can check `nvidia-smi dmon` and host iostat.
Linh: I pulled `iostat -x 1 5` and saw %util on nvme0 spike to 99% for short bursts, correlates with blocked io. Also saw `blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes` climb for tenant cgroups.
Sarah: We should also flip a conservative fallback model route for streaming to a CPU-backed lower-capacity variant for affected tenants while we stabilize. Can we route t-212 and t-88 to `model-compact-v2` read-only variant?
David: I can update routing rules in the control plane. pushing a canary policy: route where latency>500ms and tenant in {t-212,t-88} -> model-compact-v2. command: `redwood route update --selector tenant in (t-212,t-88) --fallback model-compact-v2 --apply`
Sarah: apply now. monitor for downstream errors (output quality regressions).
Priya (support): Voltix confirms streams improved after fallback routing. still seeing occasional reconnects but overall better.
IncidentBot: New events: host gw45 reported kernel OOM-killer candidate? (no kill) and several docker container restarts (non-fatal) — logged at 173912?1500.
Omar: I see a retained burst from t-88's scheduled rerank job that launched 80 concurrent workers after a previous backoff. that surge pinned NVMe and caused other tenants to queue.
Linh: Recommend: 1) add short-term rate limiter at gateway to cap concurrent model_stream calls per tenant (e.g., 20) 2) tune cgroup blkio to smoother limits (burst window) 3) long-term: move heavy batch reranks to Dedicated pools.
Sarah: Agreed. David, can you deploy gateway limiter? simple Nginx lua limiter for tenant header should be fastest.
David: deploying limiter patch to gw45/gw46 config now. snippet:
```nginx
# nginx conf excerpt
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=tenant_limit:10m rate=10r/s;
server_name streaming;
location /v1/stream {
  set $tenant_id $http_x_tenant_id;
  limit_req zone=tenant_limit burst=30 nodelay;
}
```
David: pushed and reloaded on gw45/gw46.
IncidentBot: p95=420ms p99=980ms error=0.2% (10m after throttle + route fallback + limiter).
Priya (support): Voltix reports full recovery on UX for critical workflows. They will keep monitoring and asked for a postmortem.
Sarah: Good. Now action items before unpaged:
- David: prepare host-level artifact (nvidia-smi, iostat, blkio stats) and upload to incident playbook.
- Linh: capture request traces for all affected tenants (t-88, t-212) and correlate with job schedules.
- Omar: identify which job submission triggered the burst and flag owner/team for follow-up.
- Priya: consolidate customer timeline and notify account team we will follow up with RCA.
David: uploading artifacts to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1739129999/artifacts
Linh: pulling traces and will attach in 15m.
Omar: root cause hypothesis: unbounded batch rerank job concurrently spawning many GPU workers on a multi-tenant shared pool -> NVMe saturation -> cgroup throttling -> streaming socket backpressure -> p99 latency spikes.
Sarah: for now we keep route fallback and limiter active. we'll plan an evacuation for worst offending tenant if we see >2 similar bursts in next 24h.
IncidentBot: Notice: On-call handoff scheduled in 2h. Please update `#eng-oncall` if you want to pass the incident.
Sarah: I'll take handoff but will mark as "monitoring". leaving notes in playbook.
Priya (support): Logged customer update and closed high-severity incident with Voltix as "resolved for now".
David: final metrics before demobilize: p95=260ms p99=590ms error=0.12% — trending stable.
Sarah: thanks all. we'll run a short postmortem with infra + tenant owners tomorrow. tagging Eng-Infra-Lead for follow-up. :thumbsup:
Eng-Infra-Lead: saw notes, will schedule RCA and follow up on tenant isolation policies and autoscaler quotas.
